           CYTISUS LABURNUM

         Laburnum

        (LABURNUM)


All parts of this shrub are poisonous, producing inflammation of stomach
        and intestines, with vomiting, diarrhœa, headache, paleness of face and cold skin.
        Widespread anæsthesia, and convulsions are some of the chief effects of this drug.
        Cerebrospinal meningitis. Great prostration, sense of constriction in throat, stiffness of
        nape, tearing from nape into occiput, lusterless eyes.



Head.--  Stupefaction; indifference (  Phos
        ac  ). Unequally dilated pupils;   giddiness  ;
        twitching of facial muscles (  Agaric  ). Hydrocephalus.
        Constant vertigo, intense sleepiness.



Stomach.--  Excessive thirst. Constant nausea, vomiting; burning
        pain in epigastrium.


Tenesmus and erections. Grass-green urine.



Extremities.--  Numbness and pain in hands. Difficulty in moving
        them.


Compare:   Nux; Gels. Cystine   (produces
        motor paralysis resembling that of curare and death through respiratory paralysis).



Dose.--  Third potency.
